title: Unit – 3 : Session – 1 : SLO – 1  |  Stacks — Introduction
sections: A stack is a LINEAR (LIFO) data structure.
The two main operations of a stack are PUSH and POP.
The operation that adds an element to a stack is called PUSH.
The operation that removes the top element from the stack is called POP.
The operation that returns the top element without removing it is called PEEK.
If a stack is full and a push operation is attempted, it is called OVERFLOW.
If a stack is empty and a pop operation is attempted, it is called UNDERFLOW.
Stacks are usually implemented using ARRAYS or LINKED LISTS.
In array implementation of stack, the top element is accessed using the TOP index.
In function calls, the system uses a stack to store RETURN ADDRESSES (activation records).
The initial value of top in an empty stack array implementation is usually -1.
Stack is used in POSTFIX (Reverse Polish) notation to evaluate expressions without parentheses.
A stack is also used in DEPTH-FIRST traversal of trees.
The time complexity of push and pop operations in a stack is O(1).
Reversing a string using stack works by PUSHING each character and then POPPING them.
